A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Moeen Nehzati. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendix A can be matched against the earlier main-text mathematics.

before.justification: Section VII reports original learned auction revenues and allocations in Table I and Figures 2–3, alongside analytical benchmarks.

after.justification: Section 7 reports original optimal transport maps and learned auction outcomes for two settings, presented in Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The finite-maximum parameterization and optional log-sum-exp smoothing remain. v2 omits v1's optional injective variant restricting parameter vectors to X-convex/lean functions (Sections V-B–C). This removes a proposed parameterization variant without establishing that the retained experiments' training procedure changed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates uniform-type auctions with linear valuations and no production costs. v2 retains this coverage and adds optimal transport with positive and negative quadratic costs, plus auctions with lognormal types, nonlinear valuations, quantity outcomes and production costs (Sections 7.1 and 7.2.2).

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds analytical Separate Posted Pricing, yielding 0.250 profit per good, alongside the retained SJa comparator. v1 Table I compared only with SJa, although its single-item Figure 2 already included the optimal posted-price rule.

E3.justification: The uniform-auction sweep changes from n={1,2,5,10,20} to {1,2,4,6,12,50,100,250}, and surplus/utility metrics disappear from reporting. Added experiments introduce a tensorizable OT setup and Setting B with underlying normal parameters mean 0 and standard deviation 0.25, production cost 0.1||x||₂, and n={1,5,10,20}. These are new experimental settings, not evidence of changed training budgets for retained cases.

E4.justification: v1's single-item case study comparing the learned price near 0.495 with the optimum 0.5 and its revenue curve is removed. The two-item allocation case study remains. v2 adds qualitative transport-map checks of marginal matching and displacement under opposing costs (Figure 2).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the results. Setting B's standard deviation specifies the input distribution rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: For overlapping uniform-auction cases, reported profit changes from 0.250 to 0.249 at n=1 and remains 0.274 at n=2. Other dimensions are replaced or added, including 0.450 at n=250; earlier surplus and utility results disappear. New Table 2 reports Setting B profits of 1.022, 1.202, 1.250 and 1.253 for n=1,5,10,20, respectively. Figure 2 adds OT findings under new conditions.

T1.justification: v1's Theorems 3–4 concerning lean parameterizations and convexity of the restricted parameter space are removed rather than relocated. v2 adds Theorem 5.3 and an appendix proof of smoothing approximation, including the log|Y-tilde|/tau error bound and a pointwise gradient statement; v1 asserted smoothing UAP without this proof. Kernel assumptions are refined to equi-semiconvex slices, while most foundational results and proofs are retained in Appendix A.

C1.justification: v2 withdraws the abstract and conclusion's claim that the parameterization can be made one-to-one. It expands the demonstrated application contribution from uniform multi-item auctions to optimal transport with general costs and auctions with general valuation kernels. Universal approximation and a convex parameter space remain central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability qualifications: OT requires tractable conjugation, and Setting B lacks known optimal mechanisms or strong numerical baselines. It interprets transport through displacement incentives and auction results through bundling and profit-bound sanity checks. This replaces v1's decision to avoid less-understood nonlinear and production-cost settings with qualified discussion of their reported outcomes.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses an Intel i7-1365U, 12 threads, 20 GB RAM and PyTorch, and states that both experiment types are supplied in gconvex. v1 provided the Python package and the same repository link but lacked these hardware and framework details. This is additional disclosure rather than evidence of a hardware change.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around differentiable optimization layers, bilevel mechanism learning and neural OT, adding works such as OptNet, Agrawal et al., Rahme et al. and Korotin et al. Several earlier citations and the detailed classical bundling discussion, including Armstrong and Manelli–Vincent, are removed.

P1.justification: The lengthy introductory assignment example and parameterization recipe are replaced by direct ML motivation and a contributions list. Application and conclusion passages are substantially rewritten, experiments are reorganized into OT and two auction settings, and retained mathematical properties and proofs move into Appendix A.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The main auction table is transposed and restructured, Table 2 and an OT figure are added, and the single-item figure is removed. The retained network schematic corrects +r to -r and is resized; the two-item heatmaps are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization, expands empirical evidence and makes the smoothing argument explicit. However, new Setting B uses unbounded domains despite the compactness assumption, and its piecewise constant type-gradient cannot support the allocation inversion required in Section 4.2. No workaround is documented. This unresolved validity gap in the expanded application claims prevents a reliable net-quality judgment.
